title: Europe rallies, US mixed, Indian markets set for strong open
excerpt: European equities surged while US indices closed mixed, and the rupee slipped modestly. Global cues point to a bullish start for Indian markets tomorrow despite a softer currency.

What happened

India

The Nifty 50 closed at 25,884.50 rupees, up 2.11% on the day, while the Sensex rose 2.30% to 84,328.59 rupees. Breadth was broad, with the Nifty Bank gaining 1.52% to 63,535.30 rupees and the Nifty IT posting a 4.82% jump to 33,386.95 rupees. The India VIX fell 4.89% to 16.84, signalling a retreat in market nervousness after a week of strong gains. The rally capped a November in which the Nifty has already logged a 12.3% gain, positioning it for its best monthly performance since April 2020.

Sectoral performance was mixed but tilted positive. Financials slipped 0.10% to 30,649.45 rupees and PSU banks fell 0.31% to 9,529.90 rupees, reflecting lingering concerns over credit quality. In contrast, autos edged up 0.47% to 28,623.45 rupees, pharma surged 2.84% to 29,090.85 rupees, and FMCG rose 2.82% to 49,673.55 rupees, buoyed by consumer‑spending optimism. Metals lagged 0.89% at 11,713.50 rupees, while energy ticked higher 0.61% to 36,880.30 rupees on the back of oil price movements. Realty posted the strongest gain, up 3.29% to 972.85 rupees, driven by renewed developer confidence.

Volatility eased as the India VIX dropped 4.89%, reflecting reduced fear after a series of strong earnings and foreign inflows. The IT sector’s 4.82% surge was anchored by expectations of higher software exports and a rebound in global tech spending. Pharma and FMCG benefited from domestic demand data and a softer rupee that makes imports costlier, prompting consumers to shift to locally produced goods. The modest rise in energy helped offset the metal weakness, while the real estate rally suggested confidence in the longer‑term growth story. Overall, the market’s upward thrust was underpinned by a combination of sectoral catalysts and a more benign risk environment.

Looking ahead to Friday’s open, the Indian market is likely to start higher. Europe’s FTSE 100 is trading up 1.95%, and Asian indices are modestly positive, providing a supportive backdrop. Although the rupee weakened to 92.44 per dollar, the dollar’s recent softness and a retreat in US Treasury yields should limit further pressure on equities. Domestic investors will watch the Nifty IT and pharma moves closely, while the narrowing VIX suggests that the rally can sustain momentum. Barring any surprise on the Fed’s December meeting, the confluence of global risk‑on sentiment and strong sectoral fundamentals points to a bullish opening bell.

Our view

constructive Analyst board divided (3 of 3 views)

The FTSE 100 rose 1.95% in the live European session while the S&P 500 fell 0.25% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.62% on Wednesday, creating a mixed global backdrop that frames the outlook for Indian equities. The US session remains live as global investors digest the divergence between resilient European risk appetite and softer American technology valuations. US 10-year yields closed at 4.85% on Wednesday, slipping 1.14%, while the dollar eased to 92.44 INR on Thursday, reflecting a softer greenback that reduces financing costs for Indian corporates. Brent crude is live at 91.64 USD, up 1.10%, and gold is trading live at 3597.10 USD, up 0.91%, indicating that commodity price pressures are active even as bond yields retreat. Bitcoin is live at 60549.49 USD, up 0.28%, showing continued speculative appetite in digital assets. These global flows suggest that Indian markets are likely to open tomorrow on a constructive note, supported by a weaker dollar and lower US yields, though the divergence between European and US equity performance warrants caution. The domestic Nifty 50 closed at 25884.50 INR, up 2.11%, while the Sensex gained 2.30% to 84328.59 INR, and the Nifty Bank rose 1.52% to 63535.30 INR, all signaling broad domestic strength. The India VIX fell 4.89% to 16.84 INR, underscoring reduced volatility expectations.

Sector calls

SectorCallWhy
PharmaoverweightPharma closed at 29090.85 INR, up 2.84%, demonstrating resilience within the domestic risk-on rally that saw the Nifty 50 rise 2.11% to 25884.50 INR. Lower US yields and a softer dollar improve the outlook for Indian generic exporters, while the India VIX decline to 16.84 INR signals reduced volatility that typically favours defensive sectors. The house views Pharma as an overweight candidate because it offers earnings stability amid rising Brent crude at 91.64 USD and gold at 3597.10 USD, which could pressure broader inflation-sensitive equities.
FMCGoverweightFMCG gained 2.82% to 49673.55 INR, aligning with the broad-based rally that lifted the Sensex 2.30% to 84328.59 INR. The sector benefits from domestic consumption themes even as the rupee weakened against the dollar, with USD/INR rising 0.23% to 92.44 INR, because local revenue streams offset import cost pressures. Falling US 10-year yields to 4.85% and a constructive global risk tone further support premium consumer demand.
FinancialsunderweightFinancials edged down 0.10% to 30649.45 INR, failing to participate in the broader Nifty 50 rally of 2.11% to 25884.50 INR. The risk manager highlights that a weaker rupee, with USD/INR up 0.23% to 92.44 INR, adds pressure on import-heavy banking books and could curb foreign inflows into the sector. Rising Brent crude at 91.64 USD and gold at 3597.10 USD elevate inflation and RBI tightening risks, which typically compress net interest margins.
MetalunderweightMetal slipped 0.89% to 11713.50 INR, lagging the Nifty Bank rise of 1.52% to 63535.30 INR and the broader market's 2.11% gain. The risk manager notes that rising commodities, including live Brent crude at 91.64 USD and gold at 3597.10 USD, signal inflation risks that could prompt tighter monetary policy, hurting capital-intensive metal producers. A softer dollar and falling US yields do little to offset these headwinds, while the India VIX decline to 16.84 INR suggests risk appetite is favouring defensives over cyclical commodities.
AutoneutralAuto closed at 28623.45 INR, up 0.47%, tracking a modest gain that underperformed the Nifty IT surge of 4.82% to 33386.95 INR. The sector sits at neutral status because global cues remain mixed, with the S&P 500 falling 0.25% and the Nasdaq dropping 0.62% on Wednesday, limiting export demand visibility. While the rupee weakened marginally as USD/INR rose 0.23% to 92.44 INR, import-heavy auto components face cost pressure, yet lower US 10-year yields to 4.85% support financing conditions.

What would change our view

A sustained spike in Brent crude beyond the live 91.64 USD level would validate the risk manager's caution and could force Indian bonds lower, triggering a sharper retreat in risk assets than the current constructive stance anticipates. If the rupee continues to weaken against the dollar, with USD/INR rising further above 92.44 INR, import-heavy sectors and foreign investor appetite would face renewed pressure, undermining the momentum strategist's bullish case. Should US 10-year yields reverse their recent slide and climb back toward prior highs, the macro economist's thesis of easing financing costs for Indian corporates would fracture, potentially dragging the Nifty 50 away from its 25884.50 INR close.

How the analyst board voted
  • Momentum strategist: bullish, conviction 4/5. Broad-based rally: Nifty +2.11%, Sensex +2.30% and key sectors (IT +4.82%, Pharma +2.84%, FMCG +2.82%) all surged, while India VIX fell 4.89%, signalling strong momentum and reduced volatility. Global risk tone supportive: Europe closed up 1.95% (FTSE), commodities rose (Brent +1.10%, Gold +0.91%), and US 10‑year yields slipped 1.14%, all favouring risk assets and underpinning the Indian upside. Domestic catalysts: Positive coverage of tech stocks (Tech Mahindra recommendation) and NSE’s rise to the world’s third‑largest exchange boost investor sentiment, offsetting modest weakness in financials.
  • Risk manager: cautious, conviction 3/5. European markets surged (FTSE +1.95% live) while US indices slipped (S&P -0.25%, Nasdaq -0.62%), limiting global equity momentum for Indian stocks. Commodities are on the rise – Brent crude +1.10% and gold +0.91% – raising inflation and RBI tightening risk, especially after bonds tumbled on oil price spikes. The rupee weakened (USD/INR +0.23%) adding currency pressure on import‑heavy sectors and potentially curbing foreign inflows.
  • Macro economist: bullish, conviction 4/5. Nifty 50 surged 2.11% to 25,884.50 and IT sector jumped 4.82%, indicating strong domestic momentum. US 10‑year yields fell 1.14% to 4.85% and the dollar eased to 92.44 INR (+0.23%), easing financing costs for Indian corporates. Global risk sentiment improved with FTSE 100 up 1.95% and Brent crude rising 1.10%, supporting energy and export‑linked stocks.

What to watch

  • Watch the live trajectory of Brent crude and gold as both are actively trading and could dictate inflation expectations ahead of the RBI policy review. Monitor USD/INR closely since any further weakening of the rupee beyond 92.44 INR would strain import-heavy sectors and foreign inflows.
